Gambit

GAM-bit -- two syllables, stress on the first syllable, GAM. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Gambit is a sacrificial move made to gain an advantage.

Giving away free samples all week was a gambit to draw shoppers into the brand-new store.

Worked Example

Down a goal with two minutes left, the coach pulls her own goalkeeper and sends an extra attacker forward. The net stands empty behind them -- but the swarm of attackers ties the game with forty seconds to spare.

Pulling the goalkeeper is a classic gambit: a calculated, risky move that deliberately gives something up -- a guarded net -- to gain an advantage. The word comes from chess, where a gambit offers a pawn early to win a stronger position. A gambit is bold and deliberate, never a scam and never an accident.

How Gambit Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

stratagem

stratagem: a clever plan for gaining an advantage

ploy

ploy: a carefully planned move to achieve a goal

Antonyms

blunder

blunder: a careless, costly mistake

misstep

misstep: a wrong or unwise step

How Strong Is It? — ploy → stratagem → gambit

ploy vs. gambit

ploy vs. gambit: A ploy is any planned move toward a goal, while a gambit raises the stakes: it deliberately sacrifices something real -- a piece, a point, a safe position -- to win a bigger advantage.

stratagem vs. gambit

stratagem vs. gambit: Stratagem is the strongest and grandest: a full clever scheme, sometimes with several stages, while a gambit is usually one bold opening move that sets the whole plan in motion.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — gamb-

root — gamb-: leg (Italian gamba, from Late Latin gamba 'leg, hoof')

suffix — -etto/-it

suffix — -etto/-it: little (diminutive) (Italian -etto)

Put it together

Put it together: Gambit comes from Italian gambetto, 'a little trip of the leg' -- the wrestler's move of hooking an opponent's leg. Chess players borrowed it for an opening that 'trips' the opponent by offering a pawn, and English widened it to any bold, calculated sacrifice made to gain the upper hand.

Use the root in a new word: gambol

Use the root in a new word: gambol: The lambs gamboled across the spring meadow, leaping over one another.

Root Check

Word Choice

A gambit is strategic, risky, and honest about its risk: an opening gambit, a bold gambit, a desperate gambit. It always trades something now for advantage later. Do not water it down to a mere trick or con -- a good gambit is daring, not deceitful, and the person making it accepts the cost up front.
